rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so I raise obfuscation pressure while respecting that NPB IS is a tight counting-sort kernel (rank/main/create_seq dominate runtime) where heavy control-flow transformation would measurably slow the benchmark. SUB gets the highest weights since instruction substitution has near-zero cost and applies safely to arithmetic-heavy code like rank's key computation. FLA stays high to flatten the already branchy verify/report paths, with moderate cost weights accepting its overhead in large functions like main. BCF is raised from a conservative baseline but capped, since bogus control flow multiplies both size and loop-body runtime in the hot sort loop. SPLIT and IBR provide cheap diversity on the four medium-size functions without hot-loop amplification. ICALL and IGV are kept at moderate-low weights: indirect calls and global-variable indirection carry the highest correctness risk in a program using array globals and library report routines, and previous rounds showed correctness holds only when risk-taking stays contained; the low CorrectnessRisk weights signal the selector to avoid applying them to the largest functions. Overall this shifts the mix toward low-cost arithmetic and layout obfuscation over expensive control-flow inflation, maximizing resistance per unit of overhead.
